title: Console observability: dashboard feature slice + cutmap for tracing & cost breakdown
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Purpose: produce a narrowed, launchable Console observability surface that supports initial customer needs for per-route dashboards, lightweight trace sampling, and a cost breakdown card while preserving rollback and graceful-degradation paths.

Background: multiple stakeholders asked for a broad set of observability cards (route-level KPIs, token-level cost, end-to-end traces, alerting links). Given time/resource constraints and the need for a shippable alpha, this ticket captures the PRD decisions to cut scope to an MVP slice and defines acceptance criteria and migration/fallback behavior.

Scope decisions (MVP cuts):
- Deliverables kept in MVP:
  - Route Summary dashboard card (RPS, p95 latency, error rate) with single-route filtering.
  - Cost Breakdown mini-card showing 7-day cost delta and top-3 cost drivers by model.
  - Tracing: lightweight sample capture with 1% sampling, UI link to sampled traces with search by request id and a compact flame/time waterfall view (no span-level expansion).
  - Rollout plan: canary to 5% of orgs with fallback to aggregate metrics-only view.

- Deliverables deferred (non-MVP):
  - Full trace explorer with span-level drilldown and trace retention >7 days.
  - Token-level per-request cost drilldown and token heatmaps.
  - Cross-route correlation dashboards and multi-tenant advanced filtering.
  - On-the-fly trace sampling adjustments via Console (will be config-only via infra in first release).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Keep UI surface compact to minimize frontend work and avoid high-cardinality query explosion on telem backends.
- Prioritize route-level delta and top cost drivers to give product teams immediate actionability on runaway costs.
- 1% trace sampling chosen to balance latency instrumentation overhead and signal for debugging; engineering will validate sampling telemetry impact in staging.

Open questions / clarifications requested from Eng:
- Required metrics schema changes for route tagging (ENG-20412): confirm field names and cardinality limits.
- Expected impact of 1% sampling on storage; provide cost estimate for 90-day retention if requested.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/MVP+Observability+Slice
- Mockups (Figma): https://figma.redwood.com/file/console-observability/mvp-cards
- Telemetry design doc: https://docs.redwood.com/telemetry/route-metrics-schema
- Spike repo for trace sampling (github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-trace-sampling/pull/18

Rollout & fallback:
- Canary to 5% orgs for 7 days; monitor error budget, query latency, and board-level customer reports.
- If backend query latency >50ms p95 above baseline for dashboards, automatically flip to aggregated metrics-only cards (no traces).

Post-launch: add acceptance gates to expand sampling and enable token-level cost drilldown as part of "Observability Phase II" (Q2).
decision_summary: Consolidated many small observability asks into a focused MVP: route summary + compact cost card + 1% traces. Deferred deep trace UX and token-level drilling to Phase II to reduce scope and SPIN up a low-risk canary. Approved by PM, Eng, and Design on 2025-02-13.

acceptance_criteria: Route Summary card shows RPS, p95 latency, and error rate for a selected route; data latency <= 60s for sampling window and p95 query time < 250ms on canary orgs.
Cost Breakdown mini-card displays 7-day cost delta and lists top-3 model contributors with clickable link to usage explorer (link stub enabled).
Tracing: sampled traces appear for 1% of requests with request id link from dashboard; sampled trace view loads in < 500ms and shows compact waterfall without span-level expansion.
Canary: deploy to 5% orgs; automated monitoring validates low impact (error budget unchanged) for 7 days or triggers automatic rollback.
Design sign-off recorded in Figma with final assets attached and a single responsive layout for desktop and small desktop widths.
Engineering tests: unit/integration tests for metrics tags implemented; telemetry spike validates sampling overhead <= 3% CPU for the tracer.
